title: Human Physiology and Homeostasis
notes: Homeostasis is the keeping of a steady internal state while the outside changes: temperature, blood glucose, pH, water and salts.
Negative feedback detects a change and starts a response that pushes the value back toward the set point. The response switches off as the set point is approached.
If body temperature rises, skin vessels widen and sweat increases heat loss. If it falls, vessels narrow and shivering produces heat.
If blood glucose rises after a meal, insulin promotes uptake and storage. If glucose falls, glucagon promotes release from liver glycogen. The two hormones pull in opposite directions.
The kidneys keep water and salts by varying how much is reabsorbed. Antidiuretic hormone saves water when the body is short of it.
Positive feedback, as in the intensification of labour contractions, drives a change further. It is the exception. Homeostasis of temperature and glucose is negative feedback.
importantConcepts: Negative feedback: deviation triggers response that reverses the change
Positive feedback: amplification of a response (e.g., childbirth)
Homeostatic variables: temperature, pH, glucose concentration, osmolarity
Regulatory centers: hypothalamus, pituitary gland, endocrine glands
importantStatements: Insulin lowers blood glucose; glucagon raises it.
The kidneys regulate fluid balance and electrolyte concentrations.
keyPoints: Homeostasis relies on sensor organs detecting changes and control centers responding.
Feedback loops are essential for maintaining stable internal environments.
Multiple systems work together (e.g., nervous, endocrine, muscular) to achieve homeostasis.
ADH and the kidney save water.
specialNotes: Body temperature is maintained by shivering (heat production) and sweating (cooling).
Glucose homeostasis involves insulin (lowers) and glucagon (raises) hormones.
Osmoregulation prevents dehydration by adjusting water intake and kidney function.
examShortTricks: Homeostasis = stability through negative feedback loops.
Set point = normal value that the system tries to maintain.
Sensors detect changes, control centers respond, effectors implement changes.
examNotes: Differentiate between acute (rapid) and chronic (long-term) responses.
Understand the roles of the hypothalamus (temperature, hunger, thirst), pituitary, and adrenal glands.
practiceQuestions: Explain how negative feedback maintains body temperature.

exercises.question: Blood glucose has just risen. Name the hormone and the direction of the correction.
steps: Cells take glucose up and the liver stores more of it.
The level falls back. That is negative feedback.
exercises.answer: Insulin brings a high glucose level down.

summary: Homeostasis holds temperature, glucose, pH and body water near a set point by negative feedback. Sweating and shivering manage heat. Insulin and glucagon manage glucose. The kidney and antidiuretic hormone manage water. Positive feedback is the exception, not the rule.
